thread:
alex-release: Canary live eu-west-1 at 08:42 UTC. deploybot flagged an error spike on /v1/embeddings at ~08:48. looking into blast radius; thinking small-scope mitigations first.
jamie-sre: paste deploybot signal? which metric breached?
deploybot: DeployBot: Canary signal: error_rate = 1.6% (threshold 0.7%), requests_5xx = 0.4% (threshold 0.2%), duration = 4m. Auto-rollback = TRIGGERED (note: operator override for embeddings route set to MANUAL). Suggested mitigations: reduce canary slice OR pin embeddings route to previous model.
rita-eng: reproduced locally on staging with the new quantized encoder build; looks like a quant mismatch increases false negatives. pin would be the fastest customer-visible rollback. I can prepare the pin command.
alex-release: prefer minimal blast: reduce canary slice to 2% and enable tighter retry/backoff for canary traffic. if errors stay high for 6-8m, approve pin.
cory-support: we already have two support tickets from mid-market customers reporting degraded similarity scores. engaging them now and collecting examples.
jamie-sre: throttling command to reduce slice: `trafficctl scale canary --slice 2% --route embeddings`. doing it now, will monitor.
deploybot: DeployBot: scaling canary embeddings slice to 2%. action id=f7a1e3. ETA ~20s.
rita-eng: pin command staged (no-op): `redwood route pin --route embeddings --version v1.9.0 --reason "canary error spike 6181234567"`. requires release lead approval to execute.
alex-release: I'll authorize pin if error_rate > 1.0% for another 6m. also loop in legal per rollback comms policy. @legal-bot
legal-bot: LegalBot: incident intake notified. If rollback/pin executed and customers potentially impacted, file INF ticket and notify compliance.
jamie-sre: metrics after throttle: error_rate -> 0.8%, requests_5xx -> 0.15% within ~90s. trending down but still above baseline.
cory-support: updated affected customers with a short internal note; holding public comms.
alex-release: monitor 10m. if error_rate <0.9% and stable, close as mitigated and capture in release notes as "canary transient; mitigated by traffic throttle". if it regresses, we execute the pinned rollback and post to #release-comms + #customers-affected.
rita-eng: opening rollback ticket pre-filled so we can execute quickly if needed. postmortem owner: rita-eng. runbook note added: annotate pin with `ops:annotation=emb-canary-pin-6181234567`.
jamie-sre: agree. standing by to run pin and coordinate comms.
alex-release: thanks team, keeping thread open for the watch window.
